title: fix(desktop): route broken-but-present venvs to --repair on Windows bootstrap hand-off
claim: Windows bootstrap-recovery hand-off must pick --update only for a venv proven runnable, not merely one whose python.exe/hermes.exe exist; a broken-but-present venv must route to --repair.

evidence.red: NOT APPLICABLE - the fork's target code no longer exists on MAIN. MAIN windows-hermes-path.ts:70-76: `interface BootstrapRecoverySignals { runtimeUsable: boolean }`; `chooseUpdaterArgs` returns --update only when runtimeUsable. The file-existence fields (hasBootstrapMarker/hasVenvHermes/hasVenvPython) the fork extends were removed.
evidence.green: MAIN's own test `chooseUpdaterArgs preserves the target and requires a usable runtime, not a marker` (windows-hermes-path.test.ts:42-45) asserts runtimeUsable:false -> ['--repair','--branch',...]. `npx vitest run --project electron electron/windows-hermes-path.test.ts` on MAIN: 13/13 passed.
evidence.source: MAIN main.ts:4722 `chooseUpdaterArgs({ runtimeUsable: await isSourceRuntimeUsable(updateRoot) }, branch)`; main.ts:4832 isSourceRuntimeUsable -> source-backend.ts:26 resolveSourceInstallationBackend, which execProbe()s the installation launcher with `--version` and returns null on failure. hermes_cli/main.py:704-709 imports env_loader and calls load_hermes_dotenv at module import, so a venv with python-dotenv wiped fails the probe -> runtimeUsable=false -> --repair. Landed in 5e4a2a3d24 'refactor(pm): remove legacy dependency and launch managers' (ethernet8023, 2026-09-12), after the fork's merge-base 63279301bc.

upstream_overlap: 5e4a2a3d24 (merged to main, ethernet8023) replaced the file-existence signal with a runnable probe - supersedes this fix.
#100192 OPEN nftpoetrist 'restore gateways when a bootstrap-recovery hand-off fails (Windows)' - different defect (post-failure gateway restore), no conflict.
#59204 MERGED teknium1 'probe the venv python before trusting it so Repair can escape a broken venv' - earlier sibling (resolveVenvHermesCommand).
notes: Fork patch would not apply: chooseUpdaterArgs signature changed to {runtimeUsable}. Main's probe-based gate is stronger than the fork's threaded activeRuntime.usabilityReason hint (it probes updateRoot at hand-off time). Nothing to offer upstream; recommend retiring fork #26. NOT_TESTED: no real Windows packaged run (none needed for a superseded verdict). Kanban baggage ignored.
